rows.title: What’s Working: How Colorado knows 7,322 people found jobs on state’s official job board
rows.standfirst: That’s just 2% of all who applied for a job on ConnectingColorado since last summer’s relaunch. The state job board has more than 140,000 openings. More behind the numbers.

rows.title: Cargill workers in Fort Morgan reject tentative contract to end lockout
rows.standfirst: More than 1,700 meatpackers haven’t been to work since May 20 after negotiations for higher wages and benefits broke down.

rows.title: Colorado regulators take swipe at Xcel Energy’s claims that increases aren’t that impactful
rows.standfirst: Xcel Energy uses “share of wallet” to argue customers don’t feel its rate increases. Regulators say the case is weak because Colorado’s median income is so high.

rows.title: Colorado voters will decide whether to put “right to natural gas” in state constitution
rows.standfirst: Initiative 177 seeks to prevent bans on natural gas sales and use in Colorado

rows.title: What’s Working: How Justice Ramos turned need into entrepreneurship for kids in Cortez and on the Navajo Nation
rows.standfirst: Tracy Ross Reporter Just like in a Gabriel Garcia Marquez novel, Justice Ramos was given a name that intertwines with his destiny. The 29-year-old grew up in Cortez to a mom who spent her childhood on the Navajo reservation, in the town of Rock Point, Arizona (Tsé Nitsaa Deezʼáhí in Diné) about 90 miles southwest […]

rows.title: Drop in winter spending in Colorado mountain towns has communities cutting budgets
rows.standfirst: Spending in 18 high country communities dropped to a 4-year low in 2025-26, when visitation numbers fell and snow didn’t. But towns are diversifying economies and showing resilience to bad snow years.

rows.title: Cargill meatpackers in Fort Morgan expected to take another vote on contract they rejected
rows.standfirst: Workers have been locked out of the beef-processing plant for nearly 85 days but things got worse after union strike pay was reduced.

rows.title: What’s Working: As Colorado’s minimum wage heads higher in 2027, some impact shows up in the data
rows.standfirst: Lowest-paid food workers see the biggest boost in pay. Less so for everyone else. Plus: Denver inflation at 3.9%, CU cuts job growth forecasts, the state’s first organized casino, Timnath befriends Severance

rows.title: Fort Morgan meatpackers vote “yes” on Cargill contract to end 89-day labor lockout
rows.standfirst: A push for better working conditions and higher pay left 1,700 workers with no job. Union officials said there were some gains but also it was “time to go back to work.”

rows.title: “Kingdom of Breck” campaign launches new resort-focused marketing strategy for Vail Resorts
rows.standfirst: Pushing passes falls aside as Breckenridge, Keystone lead strategic shift in resort operator’s marketing plan

rows.title: A judge told Xcel it couldn’t condemn a farmer’s land. Now the utility is headed to the state Supreme Court.
rows.standfirst: Case challenging Colorado’s largest utility’s condemnation powers could resolve conflict over 550 feet of right of way on an Eastern Plains farm

rows.title: Colorado residential electric bills will rise $5 per month — about half what Xcel requested
rows.standfirst: The state Public Utilities Commission cut Xcel Energy’s original rate hike request but the utility could ask for a rehearing

rows.title: Waymo cars will land in Denver “soon.” Here’s what you should know before hopping in one.
rows.standfirst: We’ve got details on what to expect from the self-driving car service, including a map of its boundaries, how to get on the priority list and why you shouldn’t grab the steering wheel.

rows.title: What’s Working: Colorado’s slow job growth doesn’t mean no one is hiring
rows.standfirst: Ursa Major expands and needs help; Terumo BCT shares openings and how they’re trying to fill them. Plus: Unemployment rate stuck at 3.9%, Mission Foods closing Pueblo plant, and more!

rows.title: Did 70% of Trump tax cut recipients earn less than $100,000?
rows.standfirst: Yes. Treasury reported that nearly 70% of filers receiving a tax cut from the Working Families Tax Cuts earned less than $100,000.

rows.title: Renters in this western Colorado town were almost displaced. Here’s how a public-private partnership kept them home.
rows.standfirst: When affordable housing restrictions at Eagle Villas expired, and the complex was put on the market, 120 families were at risk of losing their homes

rows.title: Colorado will get nearly $615M as Meta reaches $17B settlement with states over teen social media addiction
rows.standfirst: California, Colorado, Kentucky and New Jersey were among 29 states that sued the tech giant in 2023, but the deal cuts short the trial, which was expected to see CEO Mark Zuckerberg take the stand before a jury in federal court in California

rows.title: Tempers flare in southern Colorado as popular museum requests nearly $1M in taxpayer support
rows.standfirst: Pueblo’s City Council isn’t sure it wants to send money from an taxpayer-approved economic development fund to the Leonardo da Vinci Museum, which promised it could manage without public money

rows.title: 4 largest ski resort companies are a “cartel” scheming to raise prices, Colorado lawsuit alleges
rows.standfirst: There are now three lawsuits in Colorado’s federal court arguing that resort companies are violating antitrust laws with their pricing for passes and lift tickets

rows.title: Should Denver rip the train tracks from Welton Street in Five Points?
rows.standfirst: A community meeting Thursday night was one step in the process of deciding what to do with the light-rail tracks that run along Welton Street in the heart of Five Points

rows.title: What’s Working: Dustin Peyser built a chamber of commerce from scratch in Timnath. Then Timnath’s neighbor asked him to run its chamber.
rows.standfirst: Severance retains a separate chamber but the union is meant to be better together.

rows.title: How memories were made at county fairs in northeastern Colorado this summer
rows.standfirst: Sun reporter Jennifer Brown and photographer Cheney Orr set the scene at the various state fairs around the northeast corner, where 4-H projects, rodeos and demolition derbies bring people together

rows.title: Edgewater tested a new Colorado law that changed how much tipped workers are paid. Here’s what’s happened so far.
rows.standfirst: City Council must decide whether to keep the wage frozen or change it. If they do nothing, it’ll revert to the old formula and increase pay 25% in 2027.

rows.title: BLM will offer parcels near Aurora Reservoir for oil and gas drilling
rows.standfirst: Feds expect wells on 600 acres west of the reservoir to be drilled from a pad proposed by Crestone Peak, which is cleared for 108 wells on 32,000 acres on the state’s Lowry Ranch
